```{python}
#| label: setup
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from py.charts import show, load_json, table, INDIGO, AMBER, SLATE, SLATE_DARK, TEAL, ROSE, TEXT

s = load_json("ml-breast-cancer", "summary.json")
R = s["results"]
models = ["Decision Tree", "Random Forest", "KNN"]
best = s["best_name"]
k = R[best]
```

## Why this problem needs care

A fine-needle aspirate is imaged and the cell nuclei are measured: radius, texture,
area, concavity and so on, each summarised as a mean, a standard error and a "worst"
value. The classifier should **support, not replace, the pathologist**.

The two errors are not equal. A **false negative** (a cancer labelled benign) can delay
treatment; a **false positive** costs an extra biopsy. So the project optimises for
**recall on the malignant class** without letting specificity collapse, and checks
everything with metrics that are not fooled by the 63/37 class split.

## A leakage-free protocol

1. **Five patients were set aside first** (stratified), only to demonstrate final predictions.
2. The other 564 were split 80/20 with stratification: **451 training, 113 test**, both
   with a 37% malignant rate.
3. Imputation and scaling live **inside scikit-learn pipelines**, so their statistics are
   learned only from the data a model is fitted on. Scaling matters for KNN: feature
   ranges differ by a factor of more than 200,000.
4. Each model was tuned with **GridSearchCV, 5-fold stratified, scored by malignant-class F1**.
   The test set was used exactly once.

```{python}
#| output: asis
bp = s["best_params"]
rows = [
    {"m": "Decision Tree", "g": "criterion, max_depth 2–8/None, min_samples_leaf",
     "sel": f"{bp['Decision Tree']['criterion']}, depth {bp['Decision Tree']['max_depth']}, leaf {bp['Decision Tree']['min_samples_leaf']}"},
    {"m": "Random Forest", "g": "n_estimators, max_depth, max_features, min_samples_leaf",
     "sel": f"{bp['Random Forest']['n_estimators']} trees, depth {bp['Random Forest']['max_depth']}, {bp['Random Forest']['max_features']}, leaf {bp['Random Forest']['min_samples_leaf']}"},
    {"m": "KNN", "g": "k = 1, 3, …, 31; uniform/distance weights; Manhattan/Euclidean",
     "sel": f"k = {bp['KNN']['n_neighbors']}, {bp['KNN']['weights']}, Euclidean"},
]
print(table(rows, [("m", "Model"), ("g", "Grid searched"), ("sel", "Chosen by CV")], best=2))
```

## Results on the shared test set

```{python}
#| label: fig-metrics
#| fig-cap: "Test-set metrics at the default 0.5 threshold (positive class = malignant). Zoomed in: all models are strong."
mets = [("Accuracy", "Accuracy"), ("Recall", "Recall"), ("Precision", "Precision"), ("F1", "F1"),
        ("Specificity", "Specificity"), ("Balanced accuracy", "Balanced acc."), ("MCC", "MCC"), ("ROC-AUC", "ROC-AUC")]
fig = go.Figure()
for m, c in zip(models, [SLATE, TEAL, INDIGO]):
    fig.add_bar(x=[lab for _, lab in mets], y=[R[m][key] for key, _ in mets], name=m + (" (chosen)" if m == best else ""),
                marker_color=c, hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y:.3f}<extra>" + m + "</extra>")
fig.update_layout(barmode="group", yaxis=dict(range=[0.88, 1.0], tickformat=".2f"), bargap=0.25, margin=dict(t=50))
show(fig, 400)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-cm
#| fig-cap: "Confusion matrices on the 113 test patients (42 malignant, 71 benign)."
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=3, subplot_titles=models, horizontal_spacing=0.06)
for i, m in enumerate(models, start=1):
    r = R[m]
    z = [[r["TN"], r["FP"]], [r["FN"], r["TP"]]]
    lab = [[f"TN<br><b>{int(r['TN'])}</b>", f"FP<br><b>{int(r['FP'])}</b>"],
           [f"FN<br><b>{int(r['FN'])}</b>", f"TP<br><b>{int(r['TP'])}</b>"]]
    fig.add_heatmap(z=[[1, 0.25], [0.6 if r["FN"] else 0.05, 0.85]], x=["pred. benign", "pred. malignant"],
                    y=["benign", "malignant"], text=lab, texttemplate="%{text}", showscale=False, xgap=3, ygap=3,
                    colorscale=[[0, "rgba(148,163,184,0.12)"], [0.5, "rgba(245,165,36,0.55)"], [1, "rgba(99,102,241,0.75)"]],
                    hoverinfo="skip", row=1, col=i)
fig.update_yaxes(autorange="reversed", showgrid=False)
fig.update_xaxes(showgrid=False)
fig.update_yaxes(showticklabels=False, col=2); fig.update_yaxes(showticklabels=False, col=3)
fig.update_annotations(font=dict(size=13, color=TEXT))
fig.update_layout(margin=dict(t=40))
show(fig, 300)
```

**KNN misses one cancer, the Decision Tree two, the Random Forest three.** KNN and the
tree tie on accuracy (97.4%); KNN has the best recall, F1, balanced accuracy and MCC.
The Random Forest is the interesting case: it is *worst* at the 0.5 threshold but
*best* at ranking (ROC-AUC 0.997, log loss 0.096). Its boundary is just placed too
conservatively, so three cancers fall slightly below the cut-off.

## Over- and underfitting, made visible

```{python}
#| label: fig-val
#| fig-cap: "Validation curves from 5-fold CV on the training set: F1 on the training folds versus the validation folds."
c = s["curves"]
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=("Decision Tree: max depth", "KNN: number of neighbours k"),
                    horizontal_spacing=0.1)
for (x, tr, va, col) in [(c["depths"], c["dt_train"], c["dt_val"], 1), (c["ks"], c["knn_train"], c["knn_val"], 2)]:
    fig.add_scatter(x=x, y=tr, name="training folds", line=dict(color=SLATE, width=2, dash="dot"), row=1, col=col,
                    showlegend=(col == 1), legendgroup="tr", hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y:.3f}<extra>train</extra>")
    fig.add_scatter(x=x, y=va, name="validation folds", line=dict(color=INDIGO, width=2.5), mode="lines+markers",
                    marker=dict(size=5), row=1, col=col, showlegend=(col == 1), legendgroup="va",
                    hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y:.3f}<extra>validation</extra>")
fig.add_vline(x=bp["Decision Tree"]["max_depth"], line=dict(color=AMBER, dash="dash"), row=1, col=1)
fig.add_vline(x=bp["KNN"]["n_neighbors"], line=dict(color=AMBER, dash="dash"), row=1, col=2)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="F1 (malignant)", range=[0.8, 1.01], row=1, col=1)
fig.update_yaxes(range=[0.8, 1.01], row=1, col=2)
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="max depth", row=1, col=1); fig.update_xaxes(title_text="k", row=1, col=2)
fig.update_annotations(font=dict(size=13, color=TEXT))
fig.update_layout(margin=dict(t=70), legend=dict(y=1.15))
show(fig, 380)
```

An unrestricted tree reaches a perfect training F1 from depth 7 while validation F1
drops to about 0.90: textbook **overfitting**, so CV picked depth 5 (amber line). For
KNN, **k = 1 memorises** the training data, large k **over-smooths** and both curves
fall; k = 3 gives the best validation F1 with a small gap.

## Choosing the threshold by the cost of errors

Assuming a missed cancer costs **five times** a false alarm (cost = 5·FN + FP), the
cheapest KNN threshold was searched using **out-of-fold training predictions only**.

```{python}
#| label: fig-threshold
#| fig-cap: "Out-of-fold errors and cost for each possible KNN threshold (k = 3 gives probabilities 0, ⅓, ⅔, 1)."
t = pd.DataFrame(s["oof_thresholds"])
fig = make_subplots(specs=[[{"secondary_y": True}]])
xl = [f"{v:.2f}" for v in t.threshold]
fig.add_bar(x=xl, y=t.FN, name="missed cancers (FN)", marker_color=ROSE, hovertemplate="FN %{y}<extra></extra>")
fig.add_bar(x=xl, y=t.FP, name="false alarms (FP)", marker_color=SLATE, hovertemplate="FP %{y}<extra></extra>")
fig.add_scatter(x=xl, y=t.cost, name="cost = 5·FN + FP", mode="lines+markers+text", text=t.cost, textposition="top center",
                line=dict(color=INDIGO, width=3), marker=dict(size=9), secondary_y=True,
                hovertemplate="cost %{y}<extra></extra>")
fig.update_layout(barmode="group", xaxis_title="decision threshold on P(malignant)", margin=dict(t=50))
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="errors (training folds)", secondary_y=False)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="cost", secondary_y=True, showgrid=False, range=[0, t.cost.max() * 1.25])
show(fig, 380)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
a, b = s["threshold_results"]["threshold = 0.50"], s["threshold_results"]["threshold = 0.33"]
print(f"""
::: {{.insight}}
**What the test set said.** Lowering the threshold to 0.33 (malignant if *any one* of the
three neighbours is malignant) was cheapest on the training folds. On the test set it caught
no extra cancer (FN stayed at {int(b['FN'])}) and added {int(b['FP'] - a['FP'])} false alarms
(specificity {a['Specificity']*100:.1f}% → {b['Specificity']*100:.1f}%). The default 0.5 was kept for
the reported results; 0.33 remains the option for a clinic that values sensitivity above all.
:::
""")
```

## Does the model learn real signal?

```{python}
#| label: fig-imp
#| fig-cap: "Random Forest feature importance (top 10)."
imp = pd.Series(s["importance_top10"]).sort_values()
shape = lambda n: any(w in n for w in ["concav", "concave"])
fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=imp.values, y=imp.index, orientation="h",
                       marker_color=[AMBER if shape(n) else INDIGO for n in imp.index],
                       hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:.3f}<extra></extra>"))
fig.add_scatter(x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers", marker=dict(color=INDIGO, size=10, symbol="square"), name="size (area, perimeter, radius)")
fig.add_scatter(x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers", marker=dict(color=AMBER, size=10, symbol="square"), name="shape irregularity (concavity)")
fig.update_layout(xaxis_title="importance", margin=dict(t=50))
show(fig, 400)
```

The ranking matches clinical knowledge: malignant nuclei are **larger** and **more
irregular**. That is reassuring evidence that the models learn the biology, not artefacts.

## Final predictions on five unseen patients

```{python}
#| output: asis
fp = pd.read_csv("data/ml-breast-cancer/final_predictions.csv")
rows = [{"s": f"{r.iloc[0]} (#{r['Dataset index']})", "rad": r["mean radius"], "area": r["worst area"],
         "cp": r["worst concave points"], "p": f"{float(r['P(malignant)']):.2f}",
         "pred": r["Predicted (0.5)"], "act": r["Actual"], "ok": "✓" if str(r["Correct"]) == "True" else "✗"}
        for _, r in fp.iterrows()]
print(table(rows, [("s", "Patient"), ("rad", "mean radius"), ("area", "worst area"), ("cp", "worst concave pts"),
                   ("p", "P(malignant)"), ("pred", "Predicted"), ("act", "Actual"), ("ok", "")],
            num={"rad", "area", "cp", "p"}))
```

All five are correct. Patient 4 is the instructive one: its size is in the benign range,
but its *worst concave points* is high and only two of its three neighbours are
malignant (P = 0.67). **A borderline case like this should go to the pathologist for a
close look**, which is exactly how such a tool should be used.

## Limits, stated plainly

- With 42 malignant test cases, one patient moves recall by 2.4 points; KNN and the tree
  are within each other's CV standard deviation.
- One institution, early 1990s: performance on other equipment and populations is unknown.
- With k = 3, KNN probabilities are coarse and poorly calibrated (log loss 0.365 vs 0.096
  for the Random Forest). If calibrated risk scores were needed, the Random Forest wins.
- The 5:1 cost ratio is an assumption, to be agreed with clinicians.
